decisions.description: Withdrawals are capped by a hard-coded daily limit of 5000 per account.
The 'daily' withdrawal total is never reset, so the limit is effectively a lifetime cap per Ledger instance.
Transfers out of an account are not counted against the daily withdrawal limit.
All amounts are rounded to two decimal places (cents) using Math.round, i.e. half rounds up toward positive infinity, on binary floating-point values.
Positivity is checked before rounding, so a tiny positive amount such as 0.001 is accepted and recorded as a zero-value operation.
Amount validation uses !(amount > 0), which rejects NaN but accepts Infinity.
Balances are stored and summed as floating-point numbers rather than integer cents.
Overdrafts are forbidden: a withdrawal or transfer that would make the balance negative is rejected with 'insufficient-funds'.
A repeated transaction id is acknowledged with ok:true and ignored, without checking that the account, amount or operation type match the original.
Transaction ids are deduplicated in one global set shared across all accounts and operation kinds, kept forever with no expiry.
Amount validation runs before the duplicate check, so a retry with an invalid amount is rejected even if the id was already processed.
Rejected operations do not record their transaction id, so the same id can later be reused and succeed.
Accounts are created implicitly with a zero balance on first use by any operation, including operations that are then rejected.
Querying the balance or history of an unknown account returns 0 or an empty list rather than an error.
Failures are reported as a result object with a reason string rather than by throwing.
A transfer is recorded as two history entries, transfer-out on the source and transfer-in on the destination, sharing the same transaction id.
History entries hold only txnId, kind and amount, with no timestamp, counterparty or resulting balance.
Transaction ids and account ids are not validated, so empty or arbitrary strings are accepted.
Withdrawal checks insufficient funds before the daily limit, which determines which reason is reported when both apply.
